thread:
anna.wang: Rolling out the new continuous-batching heuristic to stable a few minutes ago (token_budget_target=32, max_hold_ms=10). Noticed p99 latency for small requests (<=50 tokens) jumped sharply after the rollout. Anyone else seeing this?

samir.patel: Yep, saw the same on the dashboard. p50 ~80ms unchanged, p99 jumped from ~120ms -> ~420ms for tiny calls. Throughput down a little too.

leo: I grabbed traces from a few affected requests. They’re spending most of the time in the batch formation path waiting on the queue condvar. The hold timer seems to let small requests sit while it waits for more tokens to fill the batch. Expected batching to help, not hurt small ones.

maya.k: Looks like the heuristic favors filling token budgets now (token_budget_target) which ends up holding 1-2 reqs for ~8-10ms on average. For tiny requests that dominates. Also saw a handful where kernel_selector falls back to a generic int8 kernel, and we get an extra memcpy. Putting snippet from pprof of a 200ms sample:```
(pprof) top 10
27.3ms 27.3ms  runtime.go:condWait
22.1ms 22.1ms  continuous_batcher.go:formBatch
18.0ms 18.0ms  kernel_selector.go:selectKernel
14.7ms 14.7ms  memcpy
...
```

deploy-bot: Deployment 2026-03-16T09:05 completed (stable rollout at 09:07).

anna.wang: Good catch on the condWait/kernel fallback coupling. Two potential levers: reduce token_budget_target for small-request routes or lower max_hold_ms so we don't wait long for fills. Also we could make the heuristic special-case single-request short sequences (<=64 tokens) to bypass fill waits.

samir.patel: I can open a quick revert to previous heuristic (token_budget_target=16, max_hold_ms=2) if we want to roll back to baseline while we iterate. Otherwise I can push a smaller tweak to bump short-request bypass. Which do you prefer?

leo: Revert on stable for now, run a canary with an explicit short-request bypass boolean. Reverting buys us time for a proper fix; the perf regression is user-visible.

maya.k: I'll run synthetic micro-bench with 10k tiny requests/sec and attach flamegraphs for both configs. Also will check KV cache hit rates — initial look shows a normalization change in the prompt preprocessor made some keys miss which increases end-to-end tokens and sometimes changes kernel selection.

anna.wang: Plan: (1) Samir do a quick rollback to previous heuristic on stable (2) Maya run the synthetic bench + KV cache hit diff and share artifacts (3) Leo prepare a short-request bypass patch for canary. Keep p99 target under 200ms for small paths.

samir.patel: Rolling back now, will update when stable is at previous config. -> :thumbsup:

maya.k: Running bench now, will post results in this thread (~20m).

leo: Thanks. Also adding a tiny config change request: log a small flag on batch formation path when hold elapsed > 5ms so we can quantify in prod without full profiling.

anna.wang: Sounds good. Tagging infra for visibility @deploy-team. :eyes:
